$comment: Charter sidecar schema. A charter is a human-readable text file (markdown) plus this JSON sidecar. The loader checks every field below and refuses to start if any check fails. Any language may be used; no language is privileged.
invariants: Exactly one charter is active at a time (see manifest.json).
The keeper refuses to start with zero active charters or more than one.
No charter may disable the honesty mechanisms (see CHARTER_INDEPENDENT_MECHANISMS.json in runtime/governance).
Charter changes are versioned, hashed, logged to the audit trail with who and when, and rollback-supported.
The governing text is always human-readable in the keeper. No silent swaps, no hidden overrides.

author.description: Who wrote or ratified this charter. A person or a community.

governing_text_file.description: File name of the human-readable charter text, in this same directory. The full text must always be readable; the hash below proves it was not tampered with and is never a substitute for the text.

governing_text_sha256.description: Lowercase hex sha256 hash of the exact bytes of governing_text_file. The boot gate recomputes this hash and refuses to start on any mismatch.

id.description: Unique charter id, lowercase letters, numbers, and dashes only. Example: charter-american-1.

jurisdiction.description: Plain-words name of the place or community this charter governs. Example: United States of America.

language.description: BCP-47 language tag of the governing text. Any language is allowed: en-US, es, fr, zh-Hans, ar, and so on. This field must never be used to rank or privilege one language over another.

ratified.description: Date the charter was ratified, YYYY-MM-DD.

version.description: Charter version, like 1.0.0. Every change to the text gets a new version and a new hash.
